title: Paloteo
summary: A Spanish stick dance performed in groups of eight in which the dancers strike their sticks together in turns.
howToPlay: Four pairs of hands hold their sticks one above the other, in a column. Strike the pair a closing ring marks, on the beat, and its sticks meet there.
The pairs are the first, second, third and fourth from the top (from the left on a wide screen).
Keep a steady count: the pattern repeats like a circle going round.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Paloteo is danced by village groups of eight who strike their sticks together in turns, in lines or in circles, to a tune.
credits: Tradition: paloteo of Spain; patterns written for this game
